 and/or will be published from time to time and that is or
 will be in the possession or control of CEIS from time to
 time, in respect of the subject matters as more particularly
 described in Schedule 1;

PROPERTY RIGHTS" design rights (whether registrable or not), any applications

 Term in the People's Republic of China:

 Content; and

 available to the public or otherwise exploit the Content in any manner

 and its affiliates world-wide.

 XFN ("AMENDED CONTENT") shall automatically vest in XFN.

 Clause 2 is set forth in Clause 4.

 Content licensed herein for accuracy or appropriateness or compliance with
 any applicable laws or regulations.

 such means of delivery or transmission as may be reasonably required by XFN
 including by online transmission.

 available to XFN on a continuous, uninterrupted real-time basis.

Source: XINHUA SPORTS & ENTERTAINMENT LTD, F-1, 2/21/2007 Hundred Thousand) for a term of twenty (20) years, in cash or such other
 consideration as the Parties may agree. The payment schedule shall be by
 five (5) instalments of US$220,000 each. The first instalment will be
 effect on condition that XFN can raise at least US$1.1 million additional
 funding in 2002.

 not and will not:
 (i) require any authorization, consent, filing, registration or
 notice of or with any government agency in the People's Republic

 order to which it is a party or to which it is subject.

 and all costs, expenses, loss, damages, liabilities, claims and proceedings
 which may be incurred or suffered by or taken against XFN in relation to:
 (a) the exercise by XFN of the rights granted herein; and
 (b) any breach by CEIS of any provision of this Agreement or any act,

 any of CEIS's officers, employees or agents and otherwise howsoever in
 connection with the rights hereby granted.

7.1 This Agreement shall take effect from the Effective Date and continue in
 full force and effect for twenty (20) years thereafter, unless otherwise
 terminated in accordance with Clause 8.
7.2 This Agreement may be renewed for an additional term of ten (10) years by
 notice in writing given by XFN to CEIS at the expiry of the Term, for a
 consideration to be mutually agreed.

 to the CEIS.
8.2 Either Party may terminate this Agreement:
 (a) if the other Party commits a material breach of this Agreement which
 is not capable of being remedied;
 (b) if the other Party commits a material breach of this Agreement which
 is capable of being remedied but not remedied within thirty (30) days
 upon receiving written notice from the non-breaching party requiring
 remedy; and
 (c) if the other Party becomes insolvent or bankrupt.

 (a) CEIS shall terminate the transmission of the Content with immediate
 effect; and
 (b) in the event that this Agreement is terminated prior to the expiry of
 the Term, XFN shall recover any sums paid to CEIS in advance for the
 unexpired Term of this Agreement, together with interest from the date
 those sums were paid until the date of full refund.

 Each Party agrees, at its own expense, to take any further action and to
 execute any further documents or instruments as the other Party may
 reasonably request to give effect to the transactions contemplated by, and
 to the terms of, this Agreement. In particular, and without limiting the
 foregoing, the Parties agree to amend this Agreement as may be necessary to
 comply with applicable laws, including without limitation the laws of the
 People's Republic of China.

 This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between CEIS and XFN and
 supersedes any prior written or oral agreement between them in relation to
 its subject matter. Any amendment of this Agreement shall be in writing and
 signed by CEIS and XFN.

 If at any time any provision of this Agreement is or becomes illegal,
 invalid or unenforceable in any respect, the legality, validity and
 enforceability of the remaining provisions of this Agreement shall not be
 affected or impaired thereby.
12. NO WAIVER
 Failure of either Party to require strict performance of any of the terms
 and conditions herein shall not be deemed a waiver of any rights or
Source: XINHUA SPORTS & ENTERTAINMENT LTD, F-1, 2/21/2007 remedies that either Party shall have and shall not be deemed a waiver of
 any subsequent default of terms and conditions thereof.

 Each party shall bear its own costs (including but not limited to legal

 and execution of this Agreement and all ancillary documentation.

 This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts all of which
 taken together shall constitute one and the same instrument.
15. NOTICE
 Each notice, demand or other communication given or made under this
 Agreement shall

 be in writing and delivered or sent to the relevant Party's Managing
 Director or General Manager at its aforesaid address (or such other address

 relevant Party shall be deemed to have been delivered (a) if given or made
 by letter by hand, when actually delivered to the relevant address against
 receipt; (b) if given or made by letter by post, two business days after
 posting; and (c) if given or made by fax, when dispatched and received in
 good order.

16.1 The English language version shall prevail in the event of any discrepancy
 between the interpretation of the English and the Chinese versions of this
 Agreement. This Agreement is governed by and shall be construed in
 accordance with the laws of Hong Kong
16.2 The Parties shall attempt to resolve any dispute, controversy or claim
 arising out of this Agreement through good faith consultation and
 negotiations. If the Parties fail to resolve the dispute through
 negotiation, such dispute shall be referred to and be resolved by
 arbitration in accordance with the UNCITRAL Arbitration Rules as may be
 amended from time to time. The place of arbitration shall be in Hong Kong.
 The language to be used in the arbitral proceedings shall be English. There
 shall be one arbitrator to be agreed by Parties. If the Parties are unable
 to agree on an arbitrator, the International Chamber of Commerce shall
 appoint one.

### Risk Assessment

#### Legal Risks:
1. **Payment** - The contract lacks a 'Payment' clause, making it difficult to ensure timely and adequate payment.

### Risk Assessment

#### Legal Risks:
1. **Payment** - The contract lacks a 'Payment' clause, making it difficult to ensure timely and adequate payment.
2. **Confidentiality** - There is no 'Confidentiality' clause in the agreement, which could lead to potential breaches of confidentiality agreements.

#### Operational Risks:
3. **Delivery** - The delivery clause is generic and does not specify any particular risks related to timing or conditions.
4. **Delivery** - The clause merely describes the method of delivery without specifying unfavorable, unfair, missing, excessive, or risky conditions.

#### Financial Risks:
5. **Intellectual Property Rights** - Representations about Intellectual Property Rights could lead to legal disputes and potential penalties.
6. **Applicable Laws and Regulations** - Warnings about compliance with laws and regulations suggest a high risk due to the potential for legal issues.
7. **Liability** - The clause imposes an excessive legal obligation on XFN, requiring them to indemnify CEIS for all liabilities arising from exercising rights under the agreement. This could be costly and potentially risky.

#### Termination Risks:
8. **Termination Conditions** - The termination clauses allow for termination based on material breaches that are not remedied within 30 days, which can lead to financial strain and legal risks due to lack of a clear remedy period.
9. **Refund and Penalties** - The clause includes a risk related to potential refunds and penalties, which could result in significant financial exposure.

#### Dispute Resolution Risks:
10. **Arbitration Rules** - The clause requires arbitration under the UNCITRAL rules, which are not universally recognized or enforceable, potentially leading to disputes being resolved outside of a jurisdiction where parties have significant interests.

### Summary
The contract contains several risks that could impact both legal and financial aspects. While some clauses provide clear protections (e.g., confidentiality), others leave room for potential issues such as non-payment, breach of intellectual property rights, indemnification obligations, and lack of dispute resolution mechanisms. The absence of specific risk management provisions in key areas like delivery timing and conditions highlights the need for additional contractual safeguards to mitigate these risks effectively.

### Recommendations
1. **Add 'Payment' Clause**: Ensure there is a clear clause detailing payment terms.
2. **Include 'Confidentiality' Clause**: Add a clause to protect against breaches of confidentiality agreements.
3. **Clarify Delivery Terms**: Specify specific conditions and risks related to delivery timing and methods.
4. **Enhance Liability Protection**: Consider adding more detailed indemnification provisions or alternative dispute resolution mechanisms.
5. **Specify Termination Conditions**: Ensure there is a clear remedy period for material breach termination clauses.
6. **Arbitration Clause**: Replace the UNCITRAL arbitration clause with one that is universally recognized and enforceable, such as ICC (International Chamber of Commerce) rules.

By addressing these risks through additional contractual provisions, the contract can better protect both parties from potential legal and financial exposure.

This Promotion Agreement (“Agreement”) is entered into effective September 10, 2015 between BookingEntertainment.com (“Promoter”) of 275

A.
VNUE hereby engages the Promoter as an Independent Contractor to secure contracts for VNUE with Thirty (30) music venues.
 
B.
The Promoter will provide certain skills, expertise, experience and abilities developed as global leader in the music and entertainment
business over two decades.
 
C.
The Promoter will consult and work with the Directors and Officers of VNUE concerning matters relating to business development
and other matters deemed necessary to perform the Promotion Services.

Based on the provided contract text and the identified risks, here is a detailed analysis of the legal and operational risks:

### Legal Risks

1. **Warranty Clause**
   - **Type:** Legal
   - **Severity:** High
   - **Clause:** Warranty
   - **Reason:** The clause restricts Promoter's authority and actions, potentially leading to legal issues if third parties believe the Promoter has the right to act on behalf of VNUE. This could result in disputes over whether the Promoter is acting within its authorized scope.

2. **Liability Clause**
   - **Type:** Legal
   - **Severity:** High
   - **Clause:** Liability
   - **Reason:** The clause imposes an excessive legal obligation on VNUE to indemnify Promoter for any liability or loss arising from actions of its officers, directors, employees, agents, or third parties not under the control of Promoter. This could lead to significant financial and reputational risks if such claims are made.

3. **Liability Clause**
   - **Type:** Legal
   - **Severity:** High
   - **Clause:** Liability
   - **Reason:** The clause imposes an excessive legal obligation on VNUE to indemnify Promoter for any liability or loss arising from actions of its officers, directors, employees, agents, or third parties not under the control of Promoter. This could lead to significant financial and reputational risks if such claims are made.

4. **Governing Law Clause**
   - **Type:** Legal
   - **Severity:** High
   - **Clause:** Governing Law
   - **Reason:** The clause creates a risk of invalidation of the entire agreement, which is not desirable. It also grants personal jurisdiction over the parties in Nevada, which may be considered an excessive or unfair contractual condition.

### Operational Risks

1. **Delivery Clause**
   - **Type:** Operational
   - **Severity:** Low
   - **Clause:** Delivery
   - **Reason:** The clause does not contain a risk but rather assumes Promoter's past experience and relationships, which is more of an assumption than a risk.

### Financial Risks

1. **Delivery Clause**
   - **Type:** Financial
   - **Severity:** High
   - **Clause:** Delivery
   - **Reason:** The payment period is excessively long (not specified in the text), increasing financial exposure for VNUE. This could lead to cash flow issues and potential penalties if payments are not made on time.

### Summary of Risks

- **Legal Risks:**
  - Warranty Clause: High (Potential legal disputes over Promoter's authority)
  - Liability Clauses (two instances): High (Excessive indemnification obligations for VNUE)
  - Governing Law Clause: High (Risk of invalidation and jurisdictional issues)

- **Operational Risk:** None identified

- **Financial Risks:** Delivery Clause: High (Long payment period increases financial exposure)

### Recommendations
1. **Review and Revise Warranty Clause:** Ensure that the Promoter's authority is clearly defined to avoid potential legal disputes.
2. **Clarify Liability Clauses:** Restructure or remove clauses that impose excessive indemnification obligations on VNUE.
3. **Restrict Governing Law Clause:** Consider specifying a more favorable jurisdiction for dispute resolution, such as where VNUE operates.
4. **Review Payment Terms:** Shorten the payment period to reduce financial exposure.

By addressing these risks, VNUE can mitigate potential legal and financial liabilities associated with this contract.
